# Kyoto 4-Day Low-Stress Plan

A calm, train-and-walk itinerary for **2 adults** from **2026-03-12 to 2026-03-15**. I’ve kept each day compact, centered on one main theme, and designed to stay under roughly **12,000 steps/day** by grouping nearby sights and using short taxi/train hops when helpful.

# Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

## Day 1: Museum + Easy Central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Kyoto Railway Museum; arrive at opening for the quietest visit.
- **Afternoon:** Umekoji Park and a slow walk to Kyoto Station area for coffee and rest.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cf/Kyoto_City_Tram_2000_2001_in_Umekoji_Park.jpg Alt=Afternoon:** Umekoji Park and a slow walk to Kyoto Station area for coffee and rest, Kyoto, Japan
- **Vegetarian lunch:** **Shigetsu** at Tenryu-ji area is ideal if you want a temple-style vegetarian meal; if staying central, choose a set meal at a modern café near Kyoto Station.
- **Dinner:** Light izakaya-style meal or noodle shop near your hotel to keep the day easy.
- **Stress level:** Low; mostly indoors with short transfers.

## Day 2: Food-Focused Nishiki + Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Nishiki Market before lunch hour for the best pace and fewer crowds.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Nishiki Market before lunch hour for the best pace and fewer crowds, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Slow food crawl toward Gion and Pontocho; keep it to 2–3 tasting stops.
- **Vegetarian lunch:** **Veg Out** near Kamo River for a relaxed plant-based meal.
- **Dinner:** Kaiseki-style or tofu-focused dinner in Gion if you want one special meal.
- **Stress level:** Moderate-low; walking is concentrated in a compact area.

## Day 3: Temples + Garden Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Kinkaku-ji early, then move on before the busiest period.
- **Afternoon:** Ryoan-ji and its rock garden, then a calm tea break.
- **Vegetarian lunch:** **Ajiro** or a simple yudofu set near temple areas for a quiet vegetarian meal.
- **Dinner:** Return to central Kyoto for an easy dinner near Karasuma or Kyoto Station.
- **Stress level:** Moderate; best done with one taxi segment to reduce transfers and steps.

## Day 4: Flexible Half-Day + Easy Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Morning:** Choose one light option: Arashiyama bamboo grove, Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds, or a café-and-river walk.
- **Afternoon:** Keep open for shopping, packing, or one last museum/castle stop if energy is good.
- **Vegetarian lunch:** **Mumokuteki Café** for a dependable vegetarian-friendly meal in a relaxed setting.
- **Dinner:** Early, simple meal near your hotel or station.
- **Stress level:** Very low; this is your recovery and buffer day.

# Budget, Pace, and Best-Value Choices

| Category | Planned Spend for 2 | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotels, 4 nights | JPY 70,000–100,000 | Mid-range, station- or Karasuma-area hotel for easy transit |
| Food and drinks | JPY 40,000–55,000 | Mix of casual meals, one nicer dinner, café breaks |
| Local transport | JPY 10,000–16,000 | Mostly trains/buses, with a few taxis to reduce walking |
| Admissions | JPY 8,000–15,000 | Museums, temple entries, small extras |
| Buffer / shopping | JPY 10,000–20,000 | Snacks, souvenirs, contingencies |
| Total | **JPY 138,000–206,000** | A comfortable target is **JPY 165,000–180,000** |

## Best ways to keep steps under 12,000/day
- Stay in **central Kyoto, Karasuma, or near Kyoto Station**.
- Group sights by area and use **taxi for one short hop/day** when needed.
- Start early, then build in a **midday café or tea break**.
- Avoid stacking too many temples in one day; 2–3 major stops is enough.
